metadata.title: E194 Holding Amazon for a Decade-Plus: Nomad's Strategy and Post-Mortem | Global 1% Investors
metadata.guest_role: Study-group presenter on Nomad Investment (Nick & Zack)

conclusion: Toby walks the 5/31 study group through Nomad Investment (UK pair Nick and Zack, incubated at Marathon): 10.2× from Sep 2001 to the early-2014 wind-down, 20.8% annualized versus MSCI World, no derivatives or leverage. The 2004–06 pivot — from 50-cents-on-the-dollar cheap assets to shared-scale compounders — put Amazon, Costco, and Berkshire at the center. Amazon was bought from 2005, 20% by 2006, doubled to 40% in the 2007–08 halving, then lifted again after the 2012 reopen. Closing the fund in 2014 froze the paradigm; the table’s warning is they stopped iterating into tech/AI.
background: Podcast cut of a 2026-05-31 closed-door on Nomad, authorized by Toby. Incremental ask versus prior letters: reconstruct actual 13F-style adds (Amazon, ASOS, Ocado, Costco, AirAsia, Berkshire) and think about life after the wind-down. Teachers: Jeremy Hosking and Marathon’s capital-cycle frame.
important_facts: Track: launch 2001-09-10, close early 2014, ~13 years, 10.2× / 20.8% annualized vs MSCI World. 2001–07 half-year max loss ≤5%; after 2008 vol and returns both rose. Two people only — Nick (~1968, UK, into Marathon in 1995 via Hosking) and Zack (Iraqi, UK 1970, Cambridge math, Jardine/Deutsche Asia through the 1996–99 bust). No sell-side, one Bloomberg, no leverage/derivatives. Early book hunted cheap assets from Asia to Zimbabwe; 2003 top-10 names were ~40%.

2004–06 thought shift: stop paying 50¢ for $1 of replacement-cost assets and instead pay $1 for a firm that can become $2/$4/$8 via shared scale economies (Rabasin’s ratio on who captures incremental surplus — customer, employee, shareholder). Costco was the teaching stock: EDLP, low markup, Sinegal culture versus Walmart/Target/Sears. Amazon from 2005, ~20% by 2006, to ~40% in the 2007–08 ~50% drawdown, then +30% after 2012 reopened to inflows — effectively buy-only. ASOS 2009 ~6% then 10%+; Ocado added into a near-halving; AirAsia one of the few full exits then buybacks (treated as a cycle). Costco saw a large trim then a 2012 add back to the 2008 peak weight.

Process: first buys already large (ASOS/Ocado ~7%, AirAsia 4% as a top outside holder). Trim a little into strength (tax), add on any meaningful dip if cash is there. Advantages Toby lists: no information edge, an analysis edge (shared-scale template), and a psychology edge (Nick’s Placebo/bridge talk). Close ~2014 → personal capital/philanthropy because they felt the craft had no more room — the room’s critique is they then missed a decade of tech/AI/bitcoin iteration. Don’t photocopy the template into a different market.

mental_model.name: Shared Scale × Buy-Only Adds × Paradigm Expiry
mental_model.components: Pay up for firms that share surplus with customers and still scale. Size the first ticket so a crash can be doubled (Amazon 20%→40%). Closing a fund can freeze the last good idea. Keep a capital-cycle cheap-asset toolkit for when the compounder set is empty.
mental_model.application: AMZN/COST still map to the shared-scale slide. Use 2008-style adds only if the thesis is scale, not a cycle (AirAsia). Treat a ‘we are done iterating’ manager as a sell signal on the process, not a reason to copy 2014 holdings forever.

key_insights.view: The 2004–06 pivot is the whole story.
key_insights.question: What changed Nomad from a cheap-asset fund?
key_insights.answer: Shared scale economies — pay $1 for a firm that can become $8 — after Costco/Amazon teaching, not 50¢ replacement-cost spreads.

key_insights.question: How did they use the 2007–08 halving?
key_insights.answer: 20% became 40%, then another 30% after 2012 inflows. That is the operating rule, not a slogan.

key_insights.view: Closing the fund froze the paradigm.
key_insights.question: What did 2014 cost them?
key_insights.answer: They felt the craft was finished and went to philanthropy — and therefore did not have to metabolize tech/AI.

top_investment_implications.thesis: Nomad’s core shared-scale holding: bought 2005, doubled in the 07–08 halving, rarely sold — medium
The teaching stock for EDLP/shared surplus; they trimmed then bought the weight back in 2012 — medium
